caption:
what is bemotrizinol, the new sunscreen ingredient in the us?

In June 2026 the FDA added bemotrizinol to the list of active ingredients allowed in US sunscreens - the first new one in more than 20 years. It covers both UVB and UVA, it is allowed at up to 6%, and the FDA says very little of it is absorbed through the skin.

"New" is relative. Bemotrizinol has been used in Europe, Australia and Asia for decades. In Korea it is permitted in sunscreens at up to 10%. The first US products using it were announced at the end of August.

What this does not mean: the sunscreen you already own did not suddenly get worse. Which filters are in the bottle matters less than how much you put on and whether you reapply. A better filter does not fix applying too little.

FDA / HHS announcement, 9 June 2026 (OTC sunscreen monograph order)
Korea Cosmetic Association ingredient database: bis-ethylhexyloxyphenol methoxyphenyl triazine, limit 10%

General education only.
